facts.raw_span: multiple painless nodules on the fingers of both hands
vesicles that ruptured and formed hemorrhagic crusts
discomfort and pain along the medial aspect of his right arm and forearm
denied trauma or insect bites
his cow had similar lesions on its teats
3–4 firm, non-tender nodules with central hemorrhagic crusts and surrounding erythema
mild tenderness and increased warmth along the medial right arm and forearm
Dermoscopy (10×) of one nodule showed an erythematous area with central ulceration and crust
yellow-white streaks, brown dots, a structureless whitish area partially surrounding the ulcer, an erythematous ring, and dot vessels

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms, including painless nodules and vesicles that ruptured and formed hemorrhagic crusts, along with the presence of similar lesions on his cow's teats, are consistent with Orf virus infection, a zoonotic disease.
The patient's occupation as a dairy farm worker and the presence of similar lesions on his cow's teats suggest a possible diagnosis of Paravaccinia virus infection, a work-related zoonotic disease.

The patient's symptoms, including painless nodules and vesicles that ruptured and formed hemorrhagic crusts, along with the presence of similar lesions on his cow's teats, are consistent with Cowpox virus infection, a zoonotic disease.

The patient's symptoms, including discomfort and pain along the medial aspect of his right arm and forearm, along with his occupation as a dairy farm worker, suggest a possible diagnosis of Erysipeloid, a work-related zoonotic disease.
The patient's symptoms, including painless nodules and vesicles that ruptured and formed hemorrhagic crusts, could be consistent with Contact dermatitis, a skin condition.
